title: Similar shapes
cover_sub: Same shape, different size. Secure the scale factor for lengths, extend to triangles inside triangles and to area and volume, then master problems that switch between all three.

levels_long.s: Scale factors and missing lengths in similar shapes.
levels_long.e: Triangles inside triangles, area and volume scale factors, and tampered evidence.
levels_long.m: Switching between length, area and volume, maps, and proving similarity.

briefing: Similar shapes have equal angles and every length multiplied by the same scale factor k. Find k from a pair of corresponding sides: new ÷ old.
Areas scale by k², and volumes by k³. To go back from areas or volumes to lengths, take the square root or the cube root.
method: Match up corresponding sides. Redraw the shapes the same way round if it helps.
Find the length scale factor k from one matching pair.
Multiply lengths by k, areas by k², volumes by k³.
Check: the bigger shape should have the bigger answers.

example.question: Two similar evidence boxes have heights 10 cm and 15 cm. The smaller box has a volume of 400 cm³. Find the volume of the larger box.
steps: = 1350 cm³. Check: bigger box, bigger volume ✓

text: A rectangle measures 3 cm by 5 cm. A similar rectangle measures 9 cm by 15 cm. Write down the scale factor.
Two shapes are similar. A side of 8 cm in the small shape matches a side of 12 cm in the large one. Another side of the small shape is 10 cm. Find the matching side in the large shape.
A photo 15 cm wide and 10 cm tall is enlarged to 24 cm wide. How tall is the enlargement?
questions.tip: Work out the scale factor by multiplying, not adding. Adding 9 cm to the height would distort the photo.

text: Are triangles with sides 3, 4, 5 and 6, 8, 10 similar? Give a reason.
questions.answer: Yes: every side is multiplied by 2.

e.blurb: A step is hidden, or there's a context to unpick. One piece of tampered evidence.

text: BC is parallel to DE. Find the length DE.
questions.working: Triangles ABC and ADE are similar. AD = 10, so k = 10 ÷ 4 = 2.5. 5 × 2.5.
questions.tip: Use the whole side AD = 4 + 6 = 10, not BD = 6. The triangles share the corner A.

text: Two similar shapes have lengths in the ratio 2 : 3. The smaller has an area of 20 cm². Find the area of the larger.
Two similar cylinders have heights 6 cm and 9 cm. The smaller has a volume of 80 cm³. Find the volume of the larger.
Two similar cones have surface areas of 50 cm² and 200 cm². Find the ratio of their heights.
Ella enlarged a shape of area 12 cm² by scale factor 3. Find her mistake.

m.blurb: No hints. Plan before you calculate.

text: Two similar bottles have volumes of 250 cm³ and 2000 cm³. The small bottle is 12 cm tall and has a surface area of 300 cm². Find the height and the surface area of the large bottle.
questions.working: Volume factor 8, so k = 2. Area factor 4.

text: Two similar solids have surface areas of 64 cm² and 100 cm². The smaller has a volume of 256 cm³. Find the volume of the larger.
questions.tip: Go back to the length scale factor first. You can't get from an area factor to a volume factor directly.

text: In triangle ABC, D is on AB and E is on AC, with angle ADE = angle ACB. AD = 4 cm, AE = 6 cm and AC = 8 cm. Find AB.
questions.working: Triangles ADE and ACB are similar (angle A is shared). AD/AC = AE/AB.

text: A map has a scale of 1 : 25 000. A lake has an area of 6 cm² on the map. Find its real area in m².
AB is parallel to DE. Explain why triangles ABC and EDC are similar, then find x.
questions.working: Vertically opposite angles at C are equal; alternate angles A and E are equal. k = 12 ÷ 8 = 1.5.

closed_points: Find a scale factor from corresponding sides.
Find missing lengths, including triangles inside triangles.
Use k² for areas and k³ for volumes.
Work back from an area or volume factor to a length factor.
